title: Data Structure
body:
[[Queue]]
[[Stack]]

---

A way of organising data so that the operations you care about are convenient. The course
builds four by hand:

| Structure | Rule | Built from |
|---|---|---|
| [[Array]] | reach any [[Index]] directly | contiguous [[Memory]] |
| [[Linked List]] | grow one element at a time | [[Node]]s and [[Pointer]]s |
| [[Stack]] | LIFO, push and pop at the top only | either |
| [[Queue]] | FIFO, enqueue at the back, dequeue at the front | either |

Two questions are being kept apart here, and keeping them apart is the actual lesson:

- **What it does** is the [[Abstract Data Type]]: the set of values and the operations, with
  no mention of how. "A stack is LIFO" is the whole specification.
- **How it is built** is the [[Implementation]]: array or [[Linked Structure]], and the client
  is not told which.

A [[Structure]] is the C++ mechanism for gluing fields together; a data structure is the
design you build with it. A [[Dynamic Data Structure]] is one that can grow at run time,
which needs [[new And delete]].

Which structure to reach for is a cost question this course cannot answer yet.
[[INFORMATION STRUCTURES]] answers it with [[Time Complexity]] and adds the rest of the family:
[[Tree]], [[Graph]], [[Hashing]], [[Binary Search Tree]].
